division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause. The better houses take the Randolph–Washington tier a block back from the trade, and the north tier under Kinzie: off the noise, on dry ground, with a garden. Inferred — the town holds one documented H roof and it is Cobweb Castle, on the north side, which is itself the clause's own outlier. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1833-11/1835-08`, which reaches 1835-08-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1834-11-05, at the Democrat of 5 November 1834, column 4, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

married.what_happened: NOT DRAWN FOR THIS HOUSE: MOVED INTO IT. The household model drew this house married and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell, so no wife was drawn. Clarissa Gilbert headed a house of her own, dealt by T-1174 to fill the women and children the age pyramid lacked; she fits this house by its own rules — her division, a band never above his, no child older than his band allows — and T-2020 folds her house into his: she is his wife here and the 2 of her house come with her. Every name, age band and seed is the one T-1174 drew; the children keep the surname they were dealt with. Both people are the town's invention at the `reconstructed` tier, and the marriage is too: no source says Elmira Fowler married anybody.

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as dress maker, milliner, at the Democrat of 5 November 1834, column 4. persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'ELMIRA FOWLER' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 5 November 1834, column 4. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `dressmaker` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Fowler, Ellen | Profession. | October 31, 1879.” (second_presb_0019, printed page 155), admitted 1879-10-31 by profession. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Fowler' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins E. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

resident_research.evidence_for: No reliable record found in the reviewed web, institutional-history, digitized-book, newspaper-index and genealogy-finding-aid searches could be tied to this 1835 Chicago person without relying on the name alone.
resident_research.notes: No candidate fact is asserted unless a source bridges the candidate to the 1835 Chicago record by more than name similarity.
resident_research.summary: Elmira Fowler is held as a candidate and not asserted: 3 Newberry genealogical-index card(s) stand under this surname on an exact-surname rule with nothing to separate the bearers; the papers carry the name 1834-11-05 as dressmaker.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('fowler_elmira:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Elmira Fowler as a dressmaker at Chicago 1 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
